about: Generated by tools/map_layout.mjs from map/world/S5.json; never edit. Metres in the section frame: X east (out of the city in S5), D north, H up. Entities keep their map IDs; figures and trees also carry their slug as id for people.json.

assumptions: The moat bridge deck is 8 m wide (north-south). This sets the depth scale for the whole section.

East-west and height share one scale, 77 px per metre (the placement test's frontal scale). With it the bridge railing is 1.2 m tall, the tax office columns 2.8 m, the passage opening 8.3 m tall, and painted street figures about 1.3x life size.

A metre of depth is the same height on the silk (51.25 px) at the gate as at the bridge. The painter draws each structure with its own receding angle, but the ground recedes up the silk at one rate: the open ground outside the gate (v 1045-1475) is as deep as the bridge deck (v 1155-1570), as painted.

Tall structures are compressed in depth beyond this: the gate tower hall is painted 3 bays wide and 5 bays along the wall (名画记), yet its east side covers only 155 px of v, which the ground rate reads as 3.0 m. Its true depth is not recoverable from the strokes (see the text map's open questions).

datum.about: the centre of the gate passage's outer (east) mouth, between its jamb feet

trees.what: Bushy clump of many long, thin, bare whips (like a coppiced willow) fanning up from the moat bank at the bottom edge of the silk, hiding the east end of the near railing, the bridgehead and the lower part of the big cart.
Another needle-cluster crown on the north bank below the building, between the grove and the big gnarled tree at u ~9445 (S4).
Slender upright bare trunk just west of the building at the top right; crown cut off by the silk's top edge.
Broad pine-like tree with dense needle-cluster crown on the north bank, its trunk mostly hidden low in the crown above a grassy bank line.
Bare tree whose trunk leans from the north-west down to the road edge; crown cut off by the silk's top edge.
Bare tree with a leaning trunk behind the road at the top of the silk, near fence posts; the crown is cut off by the silk's top edge.
Large low pine-like tree (radiating needle-cluster strokes) on the north bank of the moat; several thin trunks lean together at u 8880-8940 and the crown spreads far west over the road.

Tree at the north-west corner of the moat bridge, its trunk (about u 8500-8540) rising behind the far railing's west end. Above v 830 it spreads into dark, knobbly, twisted bare branches with clumped twig tips (elm-like), which reach east over the railing to about u 8880, mixed with fine drooping willow-like switches. It is not in leaf.

Tall willow-like tree behind (north of) the screen cart. A straight trunk (u 8340-8380) carries a dense fan of long thin bare switches radiating from a knot at about v 965, then rises to a fork at about v 570 whose limbs spread to the crown top. It is not in leaf.
Low clump of bare shrubs or saplings rising from the bottom edge of the silk, in front of the bridge's west abutment and piers. Thin straight stems, no leaves.

Huge old tree just north of the road, behind the rider. A massive bole about 85 px wide (u 8045-8130), scarred with a hollow, forks at about v 900 into several limbs. Fine drooping willow-like twigs fill the crown, and dark knobbly bare tips (elm-like) top it at v 120-200. It has no leaves, and its root flare runs east to about u 8160.
Foreground willow-like tree, crown of long thin unleafed shoots spreading from limbs that meet near [7985,1600]; it hides the porters' legs.
Bare tree in the far canopy with a dark knobbly forked head (like a pollarded willow) from which fans of thin shoots rise; trunk hidden.
Small distant willow-like crown of fine radiating shoots near the top edge of the silk, beyond the wall.

Large old willow-like tree: a thick, slightly leaning trunk splitting at about 2 m into several limbs that end in fans of long thin unleafed shoots; its crown spreads over the barber and the idlers. The man S5.fig.tree_leaner_7952 leans on its east side.
Distant tree with dense dotted dark leaf clusters (the only leafed crown here), seen beyond the wall behind the east end of the gate-tower roof; trunk hidden.

Foreground willow-like tree whose wide crown of long thin unleafed shoots fills the bottom of the silk in front of the idlers and hides their legs; the shoots radiate from limbs meeting near [7600,1540].

Old tree at the foot of the gate block below the passage mouth: a pale, pitted, gnarled trunk with a darker twisted second trunk beside it, rising to a fan-shaped willow-like crown of long thin unleafed shoots.

A gnarled, elm-like tree on the slope of the earthen wing just west of the gate block. A pale, knotted trunk with a large hollow at v ~1235-1255 rises from a flared root foot to a crown of dark crab-claw twigs without leaves. Medium-large and upright.

A big, bare, elm-like tree. Its thick, twisted trunk with pale bark patches rises from the bottom edge and splits into a left limb (up to about (6840, 1180)) and a near-vertical right limb (u ~7000, up to v 850). The crown is a dense mass of dark crab-claw twigs with knobby tips and no leaves, spreading from the lower ramp to the foot of the gate block.

An old, gnarled willow at the bottom of the silk below the ramp. A thick, light-barked trunk rising from the bottom edge sends one long limb up-left (from (6846, 1448) to (6539, 1219)) and others upward. All of them carry big fans of long, straight, leafless shoots, which fill the space in front of the lower ramp from u 6400 to 6970. Large, leaning left.
A slender young willow at the bottom of the silk: a single straight stem (visible from v 1545 to 1700) that forks at about v 1545 into a small head of fans of long, straight shoots.
A distant tree just above the tower roof's west slope. Its trunk leans right, from (6765, 138) to (6790, 88), into a broad, faint head of fine radiating shoots that reaches the top edge of the silk.
A small distant tree beside S5.tree.far_6643: a thin trunk (v 119-155). Its crown is faint and merges with its neighbours'.
A small distant tree beyond the tower roof: a thin dark trunk (v 85-127) under a faint head of fine shoots.
Fans of long, straight shoots rising from the bottom edge at the lower left (u 6470-6700, v 1640-1766), as from a pollarded willow head or young willows whose stems lie below the painted edge.

A small bare tree at the bottom left, east of the small gatehouse with the studded door. Only a low, spreading crown of dark crab-claw twigs (u 6475-6690, v 1580-1660) shows above a screen of willow shoots; the trunk is not visible.
A distant tree north of the tower, seen above its west roof end. A broad head of fine shoots radiates from a branch point at about (6520, 185); the trunk is hidden by the roof.

A willow between the tax office and the west foot of the ramp. Its dark, gnarled trunk (visible at u 6447-6474, v 717-811) forks into a big rounded head of long, straight, leafless shoots. The crown fills the space in front of the tower's west end up to the eaves. Medium-large and upright.
Tree with a broad crown of fine radiating twig sprays at the top of the silk, west of the gate tower's big pine-like tree.
Tree with a crown of fine radiating twig sprays behind the east end of the tax office's rear roof.
Small thin trunk under the spreading crowns at the top of the silk, just east of the mound tree.
Medium tree with a twisted trunk on a low mound in the open ground at the top of the silk; its crown of fine radiating twig sprays spreads mostly west.
Tree with a crown of fine radiating twig sprays (pine-like needle clusters or budding willow) rising behind the tax office's rear roof.
Bare tree with a short trunk rising behind the pile of wrapped bundles, its crown of dark twisted branches and fine twig sprays spreading west and east along the top of the silk.

Large bare elm-like tree with a thick dark trunk standing at the east end of the wine depot; the trunk rises and forks at v≈600, the west limbs spread over the depot and the inn, the east limb reaches over the tax office's roof. Leafless, twisted twigs.
Small tree with a few budding twig clusters, rising behind the ridge of the inn's upper storey; only the upper trunk and crown show.

S5.veh.covered_ox_cart_9800.name: big covered ox cart
S5.veh.covered_ox_cart_9800.what: Large two-wheeled cart with a woven-mat barrel roof over a panelled body, a big spoked wheel near its middle, a basket hung at the rear and a rolled blind or round hamper at its front; it faces east, a driver seated on its footboard, one shaft running forward to its team of three oxen (S4.ani.ox_shaft_9972, ox_far_10045, ox_lead_10235). The first of the ox carts that continue into S4.

S5.veh.cart_screen_8510.name: 串车 under the cursive-script screen
S5.veh.cart_screen_8510.what: 串车 (a barrow with one big spoked wheel under the middle) heading east, out of the city. Its load is hidden under a huge domed sheet covered in cursive-script calligraphy (the screen used as a tarp), edged by a dark band (load spans about u 8290-8500, top v 1075). One carter pushes at the rear handles and another hauls at the front shafts; a long draught pole and trace run on east to a donkey at about u 8700-8880.

painted_area.about: scan u 5600-9400, v 0-1790 (the silk's edges) on the ground; corners sw, se, ne, nw

S5.tree.elm_6580.why: its base is estimated at the silk's bottom edge, and the lower flight's foot (a builder choice below the silk) runs through it; it stands just west of the flight, which the painting hides behind these trees

S5.tree.willow_shoots_6600.why: as elm_6580: base estimated at the silk's edge, on the line of the lower flight; it stands just east of the flight

S5.str.tower_podium.why: the tower pass (the user, 2026-10-14: on the wall-top terrace you could get in but not back out): the painted upper stair starts at the terrace's south edge, right where the lower flight (马道) arrives, so there was no landing to turn east or west along the 1 m strip in front of the podium. The podium's painted front, the hall, the upper stair and everything on them move 1.1 m north (the user's fix: 'push the top part away a little'): a 1.25 m landing opens at the flight's top with the stair's run unchanged. The podium's back (estimated, hidden) stays inside the terrace's north balustrade, so podium and hall are 1.1 m shallower (blender/gate_scene.py derive)

S5.str.gate_tower.why: moves with S5.str.tower_podium (the tower pass, 2026-10-14): the hall on the podium

S5.str.tower_stair.why: moves with S5.str.tower_podium (the tower pass, 2026-10-14): the stair up to the balcony

S5.prop.tower_drum_6898.why: moves with S5.str.tower_podium (the tower pass, 2026-10-14): the drum in the hall (the builder places it 0.9 m inside the hall's back wall, which does not move, so the built drum stays where it was)

S5.fig.tower_watchman.why: moves with S5.str.tower_podium (the tower pass, 2026-10-14): he stands on the balcony beside the hall door

S5.fig.tower_balcony_man_6600.why: moves with S5.str.tower_podium (the tower pass, 2026-10-14): he leans on the balcony's front railing
